full_judgment:
Md Muzammel Hossain CJ: Since common questions of law and facts are involved in Criminal Appeal Nos. 16-18 of 2013 by leave, the Criminal Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 298 of 2012 and the Criminal Review Petition No. 18 of 2010, all these matters are heard together and are being disposed of by this common judgment.

Criminal Appeal No. 16-18 of 2013:

2. Criminal Appeal Nos. 16, 18 and 17 of 2013, by leave, are directed against the judgments and orders dated 7-1-2012,16-10-2012 and 19-1- 2012 respectively passed by two different Division Benches of the High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous Case Nos. 21084 of 2011, 14900 of 2009 and 12240 of 2009 respectively discharging the Rules in the former two Miscellaneous Cases and making the Rule absolute in the latter Miscellaneous case.

Criminal Appeal No. 16 of 2013 arising out of the Criminal Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 711 of 2012

3. Facts giving rise to Criminal Appeal No. 16 of 2013 are that the appellant as petitioner filed an application under section 561 A of the Code of Criminal Procedure being Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 21084 of 2011 for quashment of the proceedings of Special Case No. 120[2008, arising out of Gulshan Police Station Case No. 47(9)07 dated 16-9-2007, corresponding to ACC GR No. 99 of 2007 under sections 26(2) and 27(1) of the Anti-Corruption Commission Act 2004, pending before the Court No. 6 of the Special Judge, Dhaka. One Shariful Haque Siddiqui, Deputy Assistant Director, Anti-Corruption Commission (hereinafter referred as the ''ACC" ) lodged the First information Report (hereinafter referred to as "FIR") on 16-9-2007 against the accused-appellant in the Gulshan Police Station, Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) Dhaka under sections 26(2) and 27( 1) of the Anti-Corruption Commission Act, 2004 (hereinafter referred as ACC Act, 2004) and Rule 15(Gha)(5) of the Emergency Powers Rules, 2007 on the allegations that the appellant, by dishonest means, acquired in his own name and in the name of his family property worth of Taka 7,38,48,287 (Taka seven crore thirty eight lac forty eight thousand two hundred and eighty seven) only which is disproportionate to his known source of income and the appellant concealed an amount of Taka 4,40,37,375 (Taka four crore forty lac thirty seven thousand three hundred and seventy five) only in his statement of assets. Accordingly, Gulshan Police station Case No. 47 dated 16-5-2007 under the foregoing provisions of law was started against the appellant.

4. The Investigation Officer of the ACC after completion of investigation having obtained sanction from the ACC under section 32 of the ACC Act, 2004, read with Rule 15(1) of the Act Rule, 2007 and submitted the charge sheet being No. 284 dated 14-5-2008 under sections 26(2) and 27(1) of the ACC Act, 2004 and Rule 15 of the EPR, 2007 which was, accepted and cognizance was taken by the Court of the Metropolitan Special Judge, Dhaka. After submission of the Charge Sheet in due course the case was registered as Special Case No. 12 of 2008. The appellant filed an application under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure being Criminal Miscellaneous Case. No. 21084 of 2011 before the High Court Division for quashment of the proceedings of Special Case No.12 of 2008, pending before the Court No. 6 of the Special Judge, Dhaka.

5. The appellant was arrested on 13-4-2007 and continued to be in jail till 1-12-2008 when he was released on bail. On the same night he was arrested, his law chambers were raided by the law enforcing agencies and they seized a large number of papers, files, records of last 30' years, documents and deeds relating to his properties, income tax returns, bank statements, deposit receipts, bills, vouchers and payment receipts which were never returned. Before he was arrested all his bank accounts were seized and frozen by an order dated 1-4-2007 and remained so frozen till 4-3- 2009. On 3-7-2007 the ACC, respondent No.2, served a notice under section 26(1) of the ACC Act, 2004 upon him through the Jail Authorities to submit his statements of assets and liabilities within 7 days. At the same time on 5-7-2007 an order of detention was served upon the appellant for 30 days which was extended for another 90 days by an order dated 22-7-2007. While the appellant was in custody under detention, despite all the predicaments he had no other alternative under section 26(2) of the ACC Act, 2004 but to submit his statements of assets and liabilities through Jail Authorities without having any access to necessary records, bank accounts and without having any opportunity of consultation with his lawyers or concerned Chambers staff and relatives who were not allowed to see him during the period of detention.

6. A Division Bench of the High Court Division by Judgment and Order dated 7-10-2012 discharged the Rule in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 21084 of 2011.

7. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and order dated 7-10-2012 passed by the High Court Division the appellant preferred Criminal Miscellaneous Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 363 of 2012 before this Division and obtained stay.

8. Thereafter the appellant preferred regular Criminal Petition for Leave to Appeal being No. 711 of 20 12 before this Division and after hearing both the parties this Division granted leave on 19- 11-2012 giving rise to Criminal Appeal No. 16 of 2013.

Criminal Appeal No. 17 of 2013 arising out of the Criminal Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 119 of 2012

9. This appeal, by leave, against the judgment and order dated 19-1-2012 passed by a Division Bench of the High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.12240 of 2009 under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure in making the Rule absolute and there- by quashed the proceedings of Special Case No.1 of 2009 previously Metropolitan Special Case No.155 of 2008 arising out of ACC GR No. 156/ 2007 corresponding to Ramna Model Police Station Case No. 20 dated 5-12-2007 under sections 26(2) and 27(1) of the ACC Act, 2004 and Rule 15Gha(5) of the Emergency Powers Rules, 2007 read with section 109 of the Penal Code, pending in the Court No.1 of the Special Judge, Dhaka.

10. The prosecution case, in brief, is that one Monjur Ahmmad, the Deputy Assistant Director, Anti-Corruption Commission lodged the FIR on 5-12-2007 against the accused-respondent No.1 in the Ramna Model Police Station, DMP, Dhaka under sections 26(2) and 27(1) of the ACC Act, 2004 and Rule 15Gha(5) of the Emergency Powers Rules, 2007 read with section 109 of the Penal Code on the allegation that the respondent No.1 by dishonest means, acquired in his own name and in the name of his wife property worth of Taka 19,80,49,854 (Taka nineteen crore eighty lac forty nine thousand eight hundred and fifty four) only which is disproportionate to his known sources of income and which the respondent No.1 concealed in his statement of assets. Accordingly, Ramna Model Police Station Case No. 20 dated 5-12-2007 under the foregoing provisions of law was started against the respondent No.1 and another.

11. The Investigation Officer after the completion of the investigation having obtained sanction under section 32 of the ACC Act, 2004 read with Rule 15 of the ACC Rules 2007 submitted Charge Sheet being No.430 dated 30-9-2008 against the respondent No.1 under sections 26(2) and 27(1) of the ACC Act, 2004 and Rule 15(gha) (5) of the EPR; 2007 along with the sanction letter to the Court.

12. After submission of the Charge-Sheet the case record was transferred to the Court of Metropolitan Senior Special Judge, Dhaka and registered as Metro Special Case No.155 of 2008. The Metropolitan Senior Special Judge, Dhaka by his order No.1 dated 6-10-2008 took cognizance against the respondent No.1 under sections 26(2) and 27(1) of the ACC Act, 2004. On 19-1-2009 the Metropolitan Senior Special Judge, Dhaka transferred the case record to the Court No.1 of the Special Judge, Dhaka which was renumbered as Special Case No. 1 of 2009 for trial.

13. The respondent No.1 filed Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.12240 of 2009 before the High Court Division under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure for quashment of the proceedings of Special Case No. 1 of 2009 and obtained Rule and stay without impleading the appellant- ACC.

14. Thereafter, the appellant filed an application for addition of party in the Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 12240 of 2009 which was allowed by the High Court Division and the appellant was added as the Opposite Party No.2 in the Criminal Miscellaneous Case. A Division Bench of the High Court Division after hearing the parties by judgment and Order dated 19-1-2012 made the Rule absolute, and quashed the proceedings. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the aforesaid judgment and order the appellant filed Criminal Miscellaneous Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 30 of 2012 before the Appellate Division. The learned Judge-in- Chamber on 22-1-2012 after hearing the parties passed an order that the propriety and merit of impugned judgment would be adjudicated by the Appellate Division and, as such" at that stage the prayer for stay was not allowed.

15. After obtaining the certified copy of the judgment and order dated 19-1-2012 passed by the High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.12240 of 2009, the petitioner- appellant preferred the Criminal Petition for Leave to Appeal No.119 of 2012 giving rise to Criminal Appeal No. 17 of 2013 by leave of this Division.

Criminal Appeal No. 18 of2013 arising out of the Criminal Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 729 of 2012

16. This appeal, by leave, against the judgment and order dated 16-10-2012 passed by a Division Bench of the High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 14900 of 2009 under section 561 A of the Code of Criminal Procedure discharging the Rule for quashment of the proceedings of Special Case No.16 of 2008 arising out of ACC GR No.12 of 2008 corresponding to Ramna Model Police Station Case No.19 dated 10-1-2008 under sections 26(2) and 27(1) of the ACC Act, 2004 and Rule 15Gha(5) of the Emergency Powers Rules, 2007 read with section 109 of the Penal Code pending in the Court No.8 of the Special Judge, Dhaka. Relevant facts of the case are that the appellant is a Member of the Standing Committee of the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) since 1994. He was elected Member of Parliament several times from ComiIIa-2 Constituency in the National Parliament Elections since 1991. He was a Cabinet Minister of different Ministries. The appellant was arrested on 7-3-2007 by the law enforcing agency under Rule 3(1) of the Emergency Powers Rules, 2007. Subsequently, he was served with an order of detention dated 11-3-2007 under section 3(1) of the Special Powers Act, 1974 initially for a period of 30 days and thereafter, the same was extended from time to time and finally on 5-2-2007 it was extended for a period of 90 days. While the appellant was in detention he was served with a notice dated 29-5-2007 under section 26(1) of the Act directing him to submit the statement of assets and liabilities of his- own including his wife, son and daughters within 7(seven) days from the date of receipt of the notice. He submitted the statement of assets and liabilities through the Dhaka Central .Jail Authority to the Secretary, ACC, on 19-6-2007, Dhaka. He having had consultation with his lawyer on 5-6-2007 submitted the statement of assets and liabilities but for shortage of time he could not submit the statement of assets and liabilities correctly with his full satisfaction. One Md. Shariful Alam, Assistant Director, ACC lodged the First Information Report on 10-1-2008 against the accused-appellant with the Ramna Model Police Station, DMP Dhaka under sections 26(2) and '27(1) of the ACC Act, 2004 and Rule 15(Gha) (5) of the Emergency Powers Rules, 2007 on the allegation that the appellant, by dishonest means, acquired in his own name and in the name of his family members property worth Taka 9,39,67,988 (Taka nine crore thirty nine lac sixty seven thousand nine hundred and eighty eight) only which is disproportionate to his known source of income and the appellant concealed properties worth Taka 3,11,38,678 (Taka three crore eleven lac thirty eight thousand six hundred and seventy eight) in his statement of assets. Accordingly, Ramna Police station Case No.19 dated 10-1-2008 under the foregoing provisions of law was started against the appellant.

17. The Investigation Officer after completion of investigation having obtained sanction under section 32 of the ACC Act, 2004 submitted the Charge Sheet being Charge Sheet No. 411 dated 17-9-2008 under sections 26(2) and 27(1) of the ACC Act, 2004 and Rule 15 of the Emergency Powers Rules, 2007 against the appellant and others. The Chief Metropolitan Magistrate by his order dated 18-9-2008 sent the case to the Court of Metropolitan Senior Special. Judge, Dhaka wherein the case was registered as Metropolitan Special Case No. 147 of 2008. The Court of Metropolitan Senior Special Judge took cognizance under sections 26 (2) and 27 (1) of the ACC Act, 2004 and transferred the case to the Court No.9 of the Special Judge, Dhaka which was re-numbered as Special Case No. 25 of 2008. Thereafter the case was transferred to the Court No.8 of the Special Judge, Dhaka and re-numbered as Special Case No. 16 of 2008.

18. The appellant filed an application under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure being Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 14900 of 2009 before a Division Bench of the High Court Division for quashment of the proceedings of Special Case No.16 of 2008 pending before the Court No.8 of the Special Judge, Dhaka.

19. The appellant was arrested on 7-3-2007 and continued to be in Jail till 11-11-2008 when he was released on bail. After the arrest on 7-3- 2007, all the bank accounts of the appellant were seized and frozen by the verbal order of the law enforcing agencies of the Government. The cheque books and other banking documents were seized by the law enforcing agencies. Because of the verbal freezing order the appellant was unable to have access to his bank accounts. Later on, the National Board of Revenue seized and frozen all the bank accounts of the appellant by an order dated 14-1-2008. Thereafter, the appellant filed Writ Petition No. 1653 of 2011 challenging the freezing order. A Division Bench of the High Court Division on 10-3-2011 directed the National Board of Revenue to open all the bank accounts of the appellant. On 29-5-2007 the ACC served a notice under section 26(1) of the ACC Act, 2004 upon him through the Jail Authorities to submit his statement of assets and liabilities within 7 days. Earlier on 11-3-2007 an order of detention (Detention Case No. 73 of 2007) was served upon the appellant for 30 days. Subsequently the initial order of detention was extended from time to time by the Government and finally the same was extended for a period of 90 days on 5-12- 2007. The detention order was declared illegal on 5-3-2008 by the High Court Division through the Writ Petition No.9684 of 2007. While the appellant was in custody under detention, despite all the predicaments he had no other alternative under section 26(2) of the ACC Act, 2004 but to submit his statement of assets, liabilities and income on 18-6-2007 through the Senior Superintendent of Dhaka Central Jail to the Secretary, ACC, Dhaka without having any access to necessary records, bank accounts and without reasonable opportunity of consultation with his lawyers and relatives who were not allowed to see him during the period of detention. A Division Bench of the High Court Division after hearing both the parties in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.14900 of 2009 discharged the Rule by judgment and order dated 16-10-2012.

20. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the aforesaid judgment and order the appellant preferred Criminal Miscellaneous Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 377 of 2012 before this Division and obtained stay. Thereafter, the appellant preferred Criminal Petition for Leave to Appeal No.729 of 2012 giving rise to Criminal Appeal No. 18 of 2013 by leave of this Division.

Grounds of Appeals

21. This Division after hearing both the parties in all these three leave Petitions granted leave amongst others on the three following common grounds giving rise to Criminal Appeal Nos. 16-18 of 2013:

"(I) Whether the observations made by the Appellate Division in the case of Dr Mohiuddin Khan Alamgir reported in 62 DLR (AD) 290 at para 44 are mere obiter dicta.

(II) Whether obiter dictum made by the apex court is binding under Article 111 of the Constitution.

(III) Whether for initiating a proceeding under section 27(1) of the ACC Act, 2004 a prior notice is necessary and whether a proceeding under section 27( 1) of the ACC Act, 2004 is liable to be struck down for service of unlawful notice."

22. In Criminal Petition for Leave to Appeal Nos. 711 of 2012 and 729 of2012 giving rise to Criminal Appeal Nos. 16 and 18 of 2013 respectively leave was granted to consider the following grounds:

"(I) Because the decision given by the Appellate Division in the case of Dr Mohiuddin Khan Alamgir is a "law" laid down by this Court and it is not an "obiter dicta". Without conceding to the contention of the respondents that the decision of the Appellate Division is an "obiter dicta", the petitioner asserts that even then such "obiter dicta" will be binding upon the High Court Division under Article 111 of the Constitution.

(II) 	Because the High Court Division has failed to consider the law as laid down by the Appellate Division in paragraphs 44 and 45 of the said decision reported in 62 DLR (AD) 290. It is clearly stated that "the person concerned must be afforded a fair and reasonable opportunity to respond to the notice, otherwise it is no notice in the eye of law". The petitioner was in Jail when the notice was served on him and he was not allowed to come out of Jail till 1-12-2008. So the notice in question is no notice in the eye of law.

(III) Because the High Court Division has committed an error of law by giving a wrong interpretation suggesting that section 27 of the ACC Act, 2004 is independent of the notice served under section 26(1) and the proceedings under section 27(1) have no nexus with the notice dated 3-7-2007 issued by the ACC under section 26(1) of the same Act demanding statement of assets and liabilities of the petitioner. These interpretations and findings of the High Court Division are in direct conflict with the decisions of this Court reported in 62 DLR (AD) pages 277, 279 and 290. Moreover, such a decision of the High Court Division has no legal basis in view of the provisions contained in Rule 17 of ACC Rules, 2007 and the FIR and Charge Sheet submitted by the respondent No.2 affirming that the proceedings under section 27 of the Act, are based on the statements submitted by the petitioner pursuant to the notice dated 3-7-2007 issued under section 26(1) of the Act. The proceedings under section 27 are the consequence of the continuity of the process initiated by the notice issued under section 26(1) of the Act. The notice under succeeding under section 27 of the Act would be a nullity."

23. In Criminal Petition for Leave to Appeal Nos. 119 of 2012 giving rise to Criminal Appeal No. 17 of 2013 leave is granted to consider the following grounds:

"(1) For that an obiter dictum is not binding as the law declared under Article 111 of the

Constitution, it cannot be relied upon, solely.

(II) 	For that an obiter dictum is an observation by a Court on a legal question suggested by a case before it, but not arising in such manner as to require decision. It is not binding as a precedent, because the observation was unnecessary for the decision pronounced by the Court."

Criminal Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 298 of 2012

24. This Criminal Petition is directed against the judgment and order dated 20-2-2012 passed by a Division Bench of the High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 1450 of 2012 making the Rule absolute for quashment of the proceedings of the Special Case No. 33 of 2011 arising out of Sylhet Kotwali Police Station Case No.31 dated 10-2-2008 corresponding to Sylhet Kotwali G.R. Case No.120 of 2008, AGR No.2 of 2008 and E.R. No.4 of2007 under sections 26(2) and 27(1) of the ACC Act, 2004 read with section 109 of the Penal Code pending before the learned Sessions Judge, Sylhet.

25. The facts giving rise to Criminal Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 298 of 2012 are that one Md. Nasir Uddin, Deputy Director, ACC, District Office, Sylhet lodged a FIR dated 10-2-2008 with the Kotwali Police Station, Sylhet against the accused respondent Nos. 1 and 2 alleging, inter alia, that the accused respondent Nos. 1 and 2 did not give the accounts of Taka 36,38,230 in their statement of assets and liabilities dated 27-6-2007 submitted to the ACC and they had also obtained the moveable and immovable property worth Taka 11,69,25,963.69 by adopting unfair means which is disproportionate to their known source of income and they had committed the offences under sections 26(2) and 27( 1) of the ACC Act, 2004 read with section 109 of the Penal Code and accordingly, Sylhet Kotwali Police Station Case No.31 dated 10-2-2008 under sections 26(2) and 27(1) of the ACC Act, 2004 read with section 109 of the Penal Code was started. After investigation the Police submitted Police Report being Sylhet Kotwali Police Station Charge-Sheet No. 674 dated 7-9-2011 under sections 26(2) and 27(1) of the ACC Act, 2004 read with section 109 of the Penal Code against the respondent Nos. 1 and 2.

26. In this petition Mr Murad Reza, the learned Additional Attorney General, submits that since a prima facie case has been disclosed in the petition of complaint, there is no scope for quashment of the proceedings of the Special Case No. 33 of 2011 without trial. In this connection he refers to 6 BLC (AD) 93. He further submits that the High Court Division failed to consider that quashment of the proceedings at the stage before framing of charge is not permissible as per provisions of law and, as such, the impugned judgment and order is liable to be stayed. He: relies on 13 MLR (AD) 157 in support of his submission. The learned Additional Attorney General finally submits that the High Court Division failed to consider that there is no ground to maintain the application under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure and, as such, the impugned Judgment and order is liable to be set aside.

Criminal Review Petition No. 18 of 2010

27. This Criminal Review Petition at the instance of the petitioner is directed against the

Judgment and order dated 4-7-2010 passed by this Division in Criminal Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 398 of 2009 dismissing the petition and affirming the judgment and order dated 13-7-2009 passed by the High Court Division in Criminal Appeal No. 4393 of 2007 allowing the appeal and setting aside the judgment and order dated 26-7- 2007 passed by the learned Special Judge, Court No.3, Dhaka, in Special Case No.1 of 2007 convicting the respondent No.1 and sentencing him to suffer simple imprisonment for 3 years under section 26(2) of the ACC Act read with Rule 15 gha(5) of the Emergency Powers Rules; 2007 and rigorous imprisonment (RI) for 10 years under section 27(1) of the ACC Act, 2004 and to pay a fine of Taka 10,00,000 (ten lac) to the State in default to suffer rigorous imprisonment for one year more and forfeiting the properties in the name of the respondent No.1 and his dependants disproportionate to his legal source of income in favour of the State

28. The prosecution Case, in short, is as follows:-

The ACC issued notice on 18-02-2007 under section 26(1) of the ACC Act, 2004 read with Rule 15 gha (1) and (5) of the Emergency Powers Rules, 2007 under the signature of its Secretary, an Officer of the Commission, directing the respondent No.1 in jail custody, to submit statement of assets and liabilities in his own and dependants name within 72 hours which he duly complied with by submission of the statement. The Investigation Officer after completion of the investigation, submitted charge sheet to the appropriate Court along with necessary sanction for trial. During the trial, this review petitioner, examined 37 PWs and the defence. examined 7 DWs and the Court of Special Judge having taken into consideration the law and facts of the case and weighing all evidence specially, the legality of issuing of the notice with satisfaction of the Secretary, an Officer of the Commission, under Rule 15 gha (1) and (2) of the EPR, 2007 passed the judgment and order of conviction arid sentence by applying special rules of evidence i.e. presumption of guilt against the accused under section 27(2) of ACC Act and section 7 of the Criminal Law Amendment Act meaning that the accused is to rebut the presumption of guilt against him up to the Court's satisfaction.

29. The learned Special Judge, Special Court No.3, Dhaka in Special Case No. 1 of 2007 on completion of the trial having considered the materials on record and laws applicable by his judgment and order dated 26-7-2007 convicted and sentenced the respondent No. 1 to suffer simple imprisonment for three years under section 26(2) of the ACC Act read with Rule 15 gha (5) of the EPR, 2007 and rigorous imprisonment for 10 years under section 27(1) of the ACC Act and to pay a fine of Taka 10,00,000 in default to suffer rigorous imprisonment for one year more and also forfeited his properties.

30. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid judgment and order of conviction and sentence, the respondent No.1 preferred the Criminal Appeal No. 4393 of 2007 before the High Court Division in which this review petitioner was added as the respondent No.2. Before the High Court Division the appellant-respondent No.1 took 23 grounds in the Memo of Appeal out of which the 1st and the 17th are on law and the rest are on facts. In the 1st ground the respondent No.1 challenged the issuance of notice/order by the Secretary, ACC (Commission in short) under sections 26 and 18 of the ACC Act, 2004 read with Rule 15 gha (I) and (2) of the EPR, 2007 without satisfaction of the Commission ordering to submit statement of assets and liabilities followed by inadequate and untenable investigation and the entire proceedings and trial before the trial Court was initiated illegally and, as such" the impugned judgment and order dated 16-7-2007 is liable to be set aside. In ground No. 17 the respondent No.1 alleged illegality in the judgment and order of the trial court by shifting the burden of proof on the defence instead of usual onus on the part of the prosecution to prove the case beyond reasonable doubt and, as such" the entire findings of the trial Court convicting the respondent No.1 is vitiated by illegality. In the rest of the grounds the respondent No.1 raised illegality on facts of valuation of different assets and liabilities and concealment of information and possession of 6 FDRs worth Taka 1.17 crore which was not disclosed in the statement of assets and the Income Tax Returns and no legal source shown. During hearing 'the respondent No.1 raised new points on sanction asserting that three sanctions are required to be given by the Commission mandatorily.

31. The High Court Division by judgment and order dated 13-7-2009 allowed the Criminal Appeal No.4393 of 2007 and set aside the judgment and order dated 26-7-2007 passed by the learned Special Judge, Court No.3, Dhaka in Special Case No. 1 of 2007 convicting and sentencing the respondent No. 1 as stated above.

32. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid judgment and order passed by the High Court Division in Criminal Appeal No. 4393 of 2007, the petitioner preferred Criminal Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 398 of 2009 before this Division which was dismissed by the impugned judgment and order dated 4-7-2010. The present petitioner being aggrieved by the impugned judgment and order dated 4-7-2010 passed by this Division preferred the instant criminal review petition before this Division.

Submissions in Criminal Review Petition No. 18 of 2010

33. In the Criminal Review Petition No. 18 of 2010 Mr SyedAinirul Islam, the learned Senior Advocate with Mr Khurshid Alam Khan and Mr MA Aziz Khan, the learned Advocates, submits that this Court ought to consider that the impugned notice order is unauthorized until ex-post facto approval on satisfaction of the New Commission through resolution in the 3/2007th meeting on 25-2-2007 of the Commission as validated by an ex-post Jacto amending Ordinance No. VII of 2007 is accorded. He submits that the criminal proceeding is never initiated by any order/notice and the person ordered is never prejudiced inasmuch as it is a means of gathering information on the assets and liabilities from the persons concerned at the discretion of the Commission inasmuch as the Anti-Corruption Laws do not mandate issuing of notice except for alleging offence under section 26(2) of the ACC Act, and the said notice does not connote principle of natural justice and the law has only set out communication of the satisfaction of the new Commission, as such declaring a law untenable without having been assailed tantamount to legislation by the Court. He contends that this Division ought to consider that the judgment and order passed by the High Court Division has altered or supplanted the ACC Act and the Rules framed thereunder and the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 by finding that only prosecution has to prove the case inasmuch as onus lies on the accused under the special rules of evidence set out in section 27(2) of the ACC Act, section 5(3) of the Prevention of Corruption Act and section 7(1) of the Criminal Law Amendment Act. He then submits that this Court ought to consider that law allowing 72 hours time to comply with the order is not unreasonable and that the appellant having received the order complied with the same by submitting the statement of assets and liabilities, and concealed information on 6 FDRs worth Taka 1.17 crore and that his statement evidenced possession of assets of Taka 1.17 crore in IFIC Bank at Kowranbazar, Dhaka disproportionate to his legal source of income and he did not take ground of less time to submit the statement, that too he also concealed in his IT Returns while a free man as such, offence under Rule 15 gha (5) of EPR 2007 read with section 26(2) of the ACC Act is proved, and being unable to show legitimate sources of earning and possessing said assets offence stands proved under section 27(1) of the ACC Act also, and hence, the High Court Division fell into serious error of fact and law while allowing the said appeal.

34. He also submits that this Court ought to consider that the offence for possessing assets disproportionate to his legitimate sources of income stands proved under section 27(1) of the ACC Act which has got nothing to do with the notice/order dated 18-2-2007 issued by the Secretary of the Commission inasmuch as the appellant-respondent No.1 failed to rebut presumption of the trial court under section 27(2) of the ACC Act, section 5(3) of the Prevention of Corruption Act and section 7(1) of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, and hence, the High Court Division has fallen into serious error of facts and law.

35. He then submits that this Court ought to consider that the High Court Division has altered or amended the Law of Repeal as set out in sections 6, 6A and 7 of the General Clauses Act, 1897 that effect of non-ratification of an amending Ordinance No.VII of 2007 by the Parliament do not destroy amendments already incorporated in the parent law. 55. In this case the respondent No. 1 was arrested by the Joint Forces on 3-2-2007, under the provisions of Rule 16 of the EPR, 2007 and while he was in such custody, he was put under detention as per the provisions of the Special Powers Act, 1974. On 18-2-2007 the Secretary of the Commission issued an order/notice under section 26 of the ACC Act which was served. upon him on 20-2-2007 while he was in custody asking him to submit his statement of assets and liabilities within 72 hours. It is on record that all the Commissioners resigned from the Commission on 7-2-2007 and the Commission was reconstituted on 24-2-2007. On the date of issuance of notice the Commission was not properly constituted as per provisions of section 5 of the Act though the Commission was in existence as an institution under the provisions of sections 3 and 4 of the ACC Act, 2004. In order to pass an order/notice under section 26 of the Ace Act the Commission is required to be satisfied that a person has in his possession assets or acquired assets beyond his known source of income through illegal means then the Commission may by an order in writing direct the said person to submit the statement of all his assets and liabilities or any other information as directed by the said order. In the case of the respondent No. 1 the order/notice was issued by the Secretary of the Commission without having obtained any satisfaction or decision of the Commission. In that view of the matter the notice dated 18-2-2007 was defective for not having obtained satisfaction/decision from the Commission. To fill up the lacuna section 18 of the ACC Act, 2004 was' amended by inserting sub-section (2) in section 18 of the Act on 18-4-2007 by the amending Ordinance No. VII of 2007 which pro- vides for 'ex-post facto ratification of the acts done by the Officers of the Commission during the period from 7-2-2007 to 24-2-2007 when the Commission was not properly constituted as per provisions of section 5 of the Act. In this context it is pertinent to reproduce section 18 of the Act, 2004 as amended by Ordinance No. VII of 2007 which reads as under:

“১৮(১)এই আইনের বিধানাবলী সাপেক্ষে কমিশন, উহার দায়িত্ব পালনের ক্ষেত্রে কোন কমিশনার বা কমিশনের কোন কর্মকর্তাকে যেরূপ ক্ষমতা প্রদান করিবে, উক্ত কমিশনার বা কর্মকর্তা সেইরূপ ক্ষমতা প্রয়োগ করিতে পারিবেন।

(২)কমিশনের কোন কর্মকর্তা কোন বিশেষ ক্ষেত্রে, কমিশনের আবশ্যক পূর্বানুমোদন ব্যতিরেকে, ৭ ফ্রেব্রুয়ারী ২০০৭ হইতে ২৪ ফেব্রুয়ারী ২০০৭ সময়কালে, যদি এমন কোন কার্য্ সম্পাদন বা ক্ষমতা প্রয়োগ করিয়া থাকেন যাহা আইনের উদ্দেশ্যে ও কমিশনের কার্যাবলীর সহিত সংগতিপূর্ণ, তাহা হইলে কমিশন উক্ত কর্মকর্তার অনুরূপ কার্য্ সম্পাদন বা ক্ষমতার প্রয়োগকে ভূতাপেক্ষ (ex post facto) অনুমোদন জ্ঞাপন করিতে পারিবে।”

<u>56. In view of the section 18(2) of the ACC Act notice issued by the Secretary of the Commission was given ex-post facto approval on satisfaction of the new Commission through the resolution in the 3/2007th meeting dated 25-2- 2007 of the Commission as validated by the ex- post facto amending Ordinance VII of 2007, it cannot be said that the notice under section 26( 1) of the ACC Act was defective. But in this case no issue in respect of ex-post facto approval was framed, deliberated upon and decided in view of the provisions of section 18(2) of the ACC Act and in the facts and circumstances of the case the observation made by this Division in paragraph 41 of the decision reported in 62 DLR (AD) 290 as reproduced below is an obiter dicta: "If any person acts beyond his authority, to the prejudice of any person, such acts cannot be ratified or validated by post facto legislation, his action remains void." This Division misconceived the provisions of sections 18(2) and 26 of the ACC Act in observing {hat "But by sub-section (2) of section 18, the Commissioners can only ratify the 'satisfaction' of the Secretary which is certainly not stipulated in section 26. (Para-42)</u>

57. As such, the notice dated 18-2-2007, issued by the Secretary in favour of the respondent No.1, was not issued on behalf of the Commission as envisaged under section 26, and is without jurisdiction and void ab initio." (Para-43)

<u>58. The views expressed in the aforesaid observations 62 DLR (AD) 290 and 297 paragraphs 42 and 43 of this Division do not convey the correct principle of law. Because the preamble of the Anti-Corruption Commission Act, 2004 envisages that for constitution of an independent Anti-Corruption Commission, for prevention of corruption and offences relating to corruption and for enquiry into, and investigation of corruption and certain other offences and matters connected thereto the Act is enacted. Sub-section (1) of section 18 provides that subject to the provisions of this Act the Commission may, in the discharge of its duty, empower any commissioner or Officer of the Commission to do an act on its behalf and the said Commissioner or Officer would be able to exercise the said power. Sub-section (2) of section 18 contemplates that if an Officer of the Commission in a special situation without prior approval of the Commission from 7th February to 24th February, 2007 performed an act or exercised his power in such a manner which is in conformity with the purposes of the Act and functions of the Commission then the Commission may accord ex-post fact approval to such performance of act or exercise of power by the said Officer. In other words, sub-section (2) of section 18 of the ACC Act enables the Commission to accord ex-post facto approval to any act done or power exercised by the Officer of the Commission which is very much inconformity with the purposes, objectives' and functions of the Commission but not the approval of the satisfaction of the Secretary. In the instant case the order/notice dated 18-2-2007 under section 26 read with section 18 of the Act was issued in conformity with the purposes of the ACC Act and functions of the Commission when the Commission was not properly constituted as per provisions of section 5 of the Act though as an Institution the Commission was very much in existence as per provisions of sections 3 and 4 of the Act, inasmuch the Commission was having its Head Office in Dhaka and its Branch Offices all over the country. Therefore, according ex-post facto approval to the issuance of order/notice dated 18-2-2007 by the Secretary of the Commission is very much legal pursuant to the provisions of section 18(2) of the Act and in conformity with the purposes, objectives and functions of the Commission.</u>

<u>59. A provision of law cannot be struck down without examining the vires of the law having been challenged before a competent court of law. This principle of law has been reiterated in the case of Khondker Delwar vs Italian Marble Works, 62 DLR (AD) 298 and 348 para 106. In the instant case reported in 62 DLR (AD) 290 the vires of the law, section 18(2), was not challenged before a competent court of law and no issue in respect of vires of the law was raised, deliberated upon and decided by the competent court. Therefore, in a hearing of a Criminal Petition for Leave to Appeal a provision of law cannot be struck down or repealed by indirect means or by implication. The view expressed by this Division regarding the effect of section 18(2) of the Act, granting ex-post facto approval of any act done or power exercised by an Officer of the Commission during the period when the Commission was not properly constituted as per section 5 of the Act does not reflect the correct principle of law. We are therefore of the view that order/notice issued by the Secretary of the Commission was rightly ratified by ex-post facto approval on satisfaction of the New Commission through resolution in the 3/2007th meeting dated 25-2-2007 of the Commission as validated by the ex-post facto amending Ordinance VII of 2007. Accordingly, the foregoing observations and findings of this Divisions in paragraphs 42 (partly) and 43 of the decision, 62 DLR (AD) 290 and 297 do not depict the correct principle of law. In this case the issue before the court was whether the notice issued by the 'Secretary of the Commission was rightly accorded ex-post facto approval by the Commission as per provisions of section 18(2) of the Act. In view of the foregoing discussions we are convinced to hold it in the affirmative.</u>

<u>60. This Division having considered the facts and circumstances of the case rightly dismissed the Criminal Petition for Leave to Appeal No.398 of 2009 on merit by the impugned judgment and order. In the instant case relevant issues on point of law were in respect of sanction by the Commission pursuant to section 32 of the ACC Act read with sub-rule (1) of rule 13, sub-rule (4) and sub-rule (7) of rule 15 of the Rules and the order/notice dated 18-2-2007 under the provisions of section 26 read with section 18 of the ACC Act which was served upon the respondent No.1 on 20-2-2007. This Division rightly observed that the High Court Division erred in law in holding that the learned Special Judge committed illegality in taking cognizance of the offence without sanction from the Commission purportedly under section 32(1) of the ACC Act and that requirement of sub-section (1) of section 32 was complied with when the charge sheet was submitted along with a copy of the sanction letter from the Commission to the concerned court. As per provision of law, only one sanction will be required under section 32 of the unamended Act or the amended Act. In that view of the 'matter no illegality was committed by the learned Metropolitan Special Judge in taking cognizance of the case. At the time of hearing of the Criminal. Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 398 of 2009 the. learned Advocate for the Anti- Corruption Commission could not make correct submissions in assisting this Division regarding the true scope and import of section 26 read with section 18(2) of the Act and as a result an error of law crept in formulating the opinion by this Division while disposing of the leave petition with the above observations on misconceived view of law as reported in 62 DLR (AD) 290 and 297 paragraphs 42 (partly) and 43. The aforesaid observations of this Division are not tenable in law because sub-section (2) of section 18 of the Act in unequivocal terms made it abundantly clear that the Commission can accord ex-post facto approval pursuant to the amending Ordinance No. VII of 2007. In disposing the leave petition, if the opinion formed by this Division on the effect of the ex-post facto amending Ordinance No. VII of 2007 is treated to be correct, then it would amount to declaring the law ultra vires or repeal of the law, section 18(2), without examining the vires of the law by a competent court. We are of the view that declaring a law ultra vires or striking down a law or treating a law to be repealed or nullity without having assailed the vires of the law would tantamount to legislation by the court which is unknown to our jurisprudence.</u>

Secondly the Ordinance deals with two separate matters. By section 3 of the Ordinance it abolishes the posts of part-time village officers on the commencement of the Ordinance and it further declares that every person who held the post of a part time village officer would cease to hold that post with effect from that date. By section 4 and other allied provisions the Ordinance has provided regarding the creation of posts of village assistants and appointment and conditions of service of village assistants who were full- time employees of the Government. There is no doubt that a separate provision is made in section 5 of the Ordinance for payment of some amount to the ex-part-time village officers. Now by virtue of section 3 of the Ordinance all the posts of part-time village officers stood abolished on January 6, 1984 and the petitioners ceased to be employees of the State Government. These two matters became accomplished facts on January. 6, 1984, irrespective of whether the holders of these posts were paid any amount under section 5 or whether the new posts of village assistants were filled up or not. Even if the Ordinance is assumed to have ceased to operate from a subsequent date by reason of clause (2) of Article 213, the effect of section 3 of the Ordinance was irreversible except by express legislation."</u>

<u>20. We do not, however, mean to say here that Parliament or the State Legislature is powerless to bring into existence the same state of affairs as they existed before an Ordinance was passed even though they may be completed and closed matters under the Ordinance. That can be achieved by passing an express law operating retrospectively to  the said effect, of course, subject to the other constitutional limitations. A mere disapproval by Parliament or the State Legislature of an ordinance cannot, however, revive closed or completed transactions."</u>

76. Therefore, according to the Supreme Court of India an Ordinance lapses under Article 213(2) either because it is disapproved by the Legislature or it is not laid before the Legislature or because it is not replaced by Act of the Legislature, the Ordinance does not become void ab-initio and transactions which are already closed and completed in pursuance of such Ordinance, shall remain valid, until Legislature makes an Act operating retrospectively nullifying all acts done under the Ordinance. In the instant case we are of the opinion that the effect of non- ratification of an amending Ordinance No. VII of 2007 by the Parliament do not destroy/repeal amendments which have already been incorporated in the ACC Act and acts done in pursuance of the amended provisions of section 18 of the ACC Act during the validity period of the amending Ordinance No. VII of 2007 cannot be rendered invalid. Moreover, because of expiry of any temporary law by the efflux of time or the lapse of the Ordinance for non-compliance of the requirement of Article 93(2), the actions taken during its currency, as such, are passed and closed having acted upon shall remain valid untill the Parliament enact a law operating retrospectively nullifying all actions taken under the Ordinance.

<u>77. Therefore, we are of the opinion that the failure of the Parliament to pass an Act in terms of the amending Ordinance No. VII of 2007 do not destroy/repeal amendments which have already been incorporated in the ACC Act, 2004.</u>

<u>78. In respect of Criminal Appeal Nos. 16-18 of 2013 we are required to examine whether for initiating a proceeding under section 27(1) of the ACC Act, 2004 a prior notice is necessary and whether a proceeding under section 27(1) of the ACC Act, 2004 is liable to be struck down for service of unlawful notice. To answer the aforesaid question we have to decide firstly, whether the notice dated 19-5-2007 or 3-7-2007 under section 26(1) of the ACC Act is lawful or not and secondly, whether section 27 is independent of the notice served under section' 26(1) of the ACC Act and whether the' proceedings under section 27(1) have any nexus with the notices dated 3-7-2007 or 29-5-2007 issued by the Commission under section 26(1) of the Act demanding statement of assets and liabilities of the appellants in Criminal Appeal Nos. 16 and 18 of 2013 and the respondent No.1 in Criminal Appeal No.17 of 2013. As regards the 1st option in the foregoing discussions we have formed the opinion that order/notice under section 26(J) of the ACC Act is very much in accordance with the provisions of law. Regarding the 2nd option it is to be noted that section 26(1) of the ACC Act contemplates that if the Commission on the basis of any information and after holding necessary inquiry is satisfied that a person or any other persons on his behalf acquired or possessed property disproportionate to his known source of income, then the Commission may by an order in writing direct him to submit the statement of assets and liabilities and any other information as pointed out in. the said order in the prescribed manner. sub-section (2) of section 26 provides for imposition of sentence for a term not exceeding 3 years or with fine or with both on a person who fails to submit written statement or information in respect of assets and liabilities or supplies false or baseless information and documents in violation of the order pursuant to section 26(1) of the ACC Act. Whereas section 27 of the ACC Act provides for maximum sentence of 10 years and minimum 3 years imprisonment for acquiring/amassing property beyond known source of income and the property in question be confiscated if he fails to explain satisfactorily to the court in the trial in respect of acquisition or amassing of the property. Generally, no notice is required to be served upon a person before instituting a criminal proceeding against him. Moreover, section 27 does not envisage any notice to be served upon the person before initiation of a criminal proceeding under the section. In other words, there is nothing in section 27 requiring service of any prior notice before initiation of a criminal proceeding. Therefore, section 27 is independent of the notice served under section 26( 1) of the ACC Act and the proceedings under section 27(1) have no. nexus with the notice served by the ACC under section 26(1) of the ACC Act demanding statement of assets and liabilities of the accused appellants in criminal Appeal Nos. 16 and 18 of 2013 and the accused respondent No.1 in Criminal Appeal No. 17 of 2013. The established principle of law is that if the law enforcing agency knows that a person has committed an offence or there are sufficient reasons to believe that the person has committed an offence, then the law enforcing agency is empowered to institute a criminal proceeding against him and no notice is required to be served upon him before initiation of the same against him. This view has been aptly expressed in the decision of this Division in the case of ACC vs Iqbal Hasan Mahmud reported in 66 DLR (AD) 185 wherein we observed as under: "Section 27 is an independent provision and for initiation of a proceeding against any person under the said provision no notice is required to be 'served. If the prosecution can establish that any person has acquired or amassed wealth which is beyond his known source of income, he may be prosecuted and convicted under section 27(1)".</u>

<u>79. We have already discussed the purpose, intendment and scheme of the ACC Act, 2004. From the scheme and contents of the Act it appears that section 26 and section 27 of the ACC Act are independent from each other and there is no nexus between these two sections. Section 27 being an independent section provides that if there are sufficient reasons to think that a person has acquired or amassed property illegally which is beyond his known source of income then he may be sentenced to suffer imprisonment for a term not more than 10 years and not less than 3 years and to pay fine and the property in question is liable to be confiscated. Therefore, there is no difficulty to say that before issuance of any notice under section 26 of the ACC Act upon a person the Commission must have knowledge that the said person has acquired property' beyond known source of income. In other words, the fact of acquiring property beyond some one's known source of income was within the knowledge of the Commission long before the issuance of the order notice under, section 26 of the Act. Section 27 of the ACC Act is independent of the notice served under section 26(1) of the ACC Act. Therefore, in the instant cases the proceedings under section 27(1) have no nexus with the notices dated 3-7-2007 or 29-5-2007 issued under section 26(1) of the ACC Act.</u>

80. We have noticed that in all these three appeals notices were issued under section 26(1) of the ACC Act by the Secretary of the Commission upon the accused appellants in Criminal Appeal Nos. 16 and 18 of 20. 13 and the accused respondent No.1 in Criminal Appeal No.17 of 2013 to submit their statements of assets and liabilities when they were in custody. It appears that all these accused appellants in the two former appeals or the accused respondent No.1 in the latter appeal submitted their statements of assets and liabilities to the ACC without raising any objection or difficulty as to their position in custody.

<u>81. The observation made by this Division in the case of ACC vs Dr Mohiuddin Khan Alamgir reported in 62 DLR (AD) 290 in Para 41 is an obiter dicta which is not binding upon the parties. The observation made in Para 42 to the effect that "But by sub-section (2) of section 18, the Commissioners can only ratify the satisfaction of the Secretary which' is certainly not stipulated in section 26." and in Para 43 to the effect that" as such, the notice dated 18-2-2007 issued by the Secretary in favour of the respondent No.1 was not issued on behalf of the Commission as envisaged under section 26 and is without jurisdiction and void abinitio." are wrong in principle and misconceived in law and, as such, the aforesaid observations of this Division in the reported decision cannot be justified in the facts and circumstances of the case and the relevant provisions of law and, as such, these observations have no legal basis.</u>

82. In respect of the differed judgments and orders passed by the High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous. Case No. 21084 of 2011 and Criminal Miscellaneous No. 14900 of 2009 without referring the matter to a larger Bench for decisions as per provisions of the Rule I of Chapter VII of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh (High Court Division) Rules, 1973 and in view of the judgments and orders passed by different Division Benches of the High Court Division relying on the decisions reported in 62 DLR (AD) 277, 279 and 290, it is to be noted that this Division consistently held that if a single Bench wants to differ from the decision of another single Bench or a Division Bench wants to differ from the decision of another Division Bench then the matter should be referred to the learned Chief Justice for constituting an appropriate Bench for resolving the dispute. However, Rule 1 of Chapter VII of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh (High Court Division) Rules, 1973 also envisages that whenever a High Court Division differs from any other Division on appoint of law, the case shall be referred to the learned Chief Justice for decision by a Full Bench. The provisions of the Rule 1 of Chapter VII of the Rules no doubt is binding on all Benches of the High Court Division faced with such a situation of conflicting decisions. We have already observed that an observation by the way in a judgment which is not necessary for the decision of the case is an obiter dictum which cannot operate as a binding precedent under Article 111 of the Constitution. In the instant cases under consideration the High Court Division having considered the aforesaid' decisions of the Appellate Division found that these are obiter dictum not ratio decidendi of the cases and, as such, these are not binding precedents under Article 111 of the Constitution on the High Court Division in deciding a case under consideration. While dealing with an observation of the Appellate Division which is an obiter dictum of the case, though not being a binding precedent is worthy of respect and considerable weight. Therefore, the High Court Division is expected to be very cautious while dealing with an observation of the Appellate Division. Even in the case of a decision given per incuriam the High Court Division should assign sufficient reasons while feeling unable to follow the said decisions. In the instant case the High Court Division has assigned sufficient reasons in the aforesaid two miscellaneous cases in discharging the Rules.

83. In view of the foregoing discussions, the observation made by this Division in the case of Anti-Corruption Commission vs Shamima Begum reported in 62 DLR (AD) 277 and 279 Para-S and in the case of Anti-Corruption Commission vs Nargis Begum reported in 62 DLR (AD) 279 and 280 paragraph 9 to the' effect that "Similarly, offence under section 27(1) of the ACC Act, 2004 is an aggravated form of the offence under section 26(2) for acquisition of assets movable and immovable in the name of person or others dependent on him when he fails to explain such acquisition. This person is definitely a person who was asked under section 26(1) of the ACC- Act, 2004 to submit statement of assets. In the absence of any statement of assets there was no scope for him to submit any explanation for acquisition of the assets. No citizen could be arraigned for such a severe offence' in absence of service of any notice or order for explaining the source of income. Offence of abetment under section 109 is equally could not be conceived of with regard to such an offence" is wrong in principle and this observation does not depict the correct principle of law in view of the foregoing discussions. Moreover, the observation made by the High Court Division as noted by this Division in the case of Anti-Corruption Commission vs Shamima Begum reported in 62 DLR (AD) 277 and 279 Para- 9 to the effect that no such offence of abetment under section 109 of the Penal Code could be conceived of in respect of an offence under section 26(2) or 27(1) of the ACC Act, 2004 and observation made by this Division to the effect that "Accordingly, lodging of FIR, taking cognizance, initiation of criminal proceedings against the writ-petitioners are unwarranted, unauthorized and without jurisdiction" also do not depict the correct principle of law. Therefore, in Criminal Miscellaneous case Nos. 21084 of 2011 and 14900 of 2009 the High Court Division having considered the facts and circumstances of the cases and the principle of law involved came to correct decisions in discharging the Rules. But in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 12240 of 2009 the High Court Division misconstrued the provisions of law and came to a wrong decision in making the Rule absolute.
